summary: Reviewed 116 acceptance criteria. Host withheld 18 unsupported criterion decisions and 3 invalid issue updates. See the retained model proposal and effective coverage for details.

requirements.description: Time Loop is a per-level 30-second time-loop platformer: every level has a 30-second active loop duration before rewind.
requirements.source_excerpt: Each level is a 30-second loop.
acceptance_criteria: Entering any level initializes a visible countdown at 30 seconds.
The active loop expires after exactly 30 seconds of gameplay time at the configured simulation rate.
All 24 levels use the same 30-second loop duration.

requirements.description: When the loop timer expires, the player is rewound and a ghost of the previous loop replays simultaneously.
requirements.source_excerpt: player starts again — but a ghost of the previous loop replays simultaneously
acceptance_criteria: At timer expiry the current player is restored to the level spawn point.
A ghost instance is created at the spawn point and begins replaying the previous loop from t=0.
Ghost movement and actions correspond to the recorded player state at the same loop time.

requirements.description: Ghosts can hold switches, distract enemies, and stand on pressure plates while the current player pursues other objectives.
requirements.source_excerpt:
The ghost can hold switches, distract enemies, or
stand on pressure plates while the current player tackles other objectives.
acceptance_criteria: Ghost occupancy of a switch or pressure plate counts as held while the ghost remains on it.
Enemies within the defined distraction range enter a distracted state while a ghost is near.
These ghost interactions can occur concurrently with independent player actions elsewhere in the level.

requirements.description: Loops layer so prior-loop ghosts can cooperate with the current player and with each other to solve a level.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Multiple loops layer: loop 1's ghost holds a door open, loop 2's ghost stands
on a platform to create a bridge, and in loop 3 the player finally reaches the
exit using both ghosts' contributions.
acceptance_criteria: At least one authored level requires simultaneous contributions from two prior ghosts before the current player can reach the exit.
Removing either required ghost contribution makes the exit unreachable.
Ghost contributions persist across subsequent loops until reset or the maximum loop limit is reached.

requirements.description: The puzzle design is temporal coordination: the player plans what each loop-self must do and when so all versions cooperate across time.
requirements.source_excerpt:
The puzzle is temporal coordination —
planning what each loop-self needs to do and when, so that all versions
cooperate across time.
acceptance_criteria: At least one level cannot be solved in a single loop.
The authored solution requires scheduling distinct actions in different loop iterations at specified times.
Earlier-loop ghost actions are necessary for later-loop success.

requirements.description: The game contains twenty-four levels across four chapters, escalating from single-ghost puzzles to four-loop orchestrations.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Twenty-four levels across four chapters escalate from
single-ghost puzzles to four-loop orchestrations.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly 24 playable levels are defined in level data.
The levels are grouped into four chapters with six levels per chapter.
Chapter 1 levels require at most one ghost; the final chapter includes levels requiring four active loops.

verification.rationale: Criterion 2: Chapter 1 uses max_ghosts=1 but no level data distinguishes progressive escalation and no level requires four active loops; max_ghosts returns 1/2/3/3 with identical geometry, so the escalation to four-loop orchestrations is not implemented.

requirements.description: The title screen visually shows overlapping clock hands and ghost silhouettes.
requirements.source_excerpt: A title screen shows overlapping clock hands and ghost silhouettes.
acceptance_criteria: The ordinary launch title screen displays at least two overlapping clock-hand graphics.
Ghost silhouettes are visible on the title screen.
The title screen is the first ordinary-entry screen before menus.

requirements.description: A chapter menu reveals four chapters, each containing six levels.
requirements.source_excerpt:
A chapter
menu reveals four chapters of six levels each.
acceptance_criteria: The chapter menu presents four chapter entries.
Each chapter entry exposes six level entries, for 24 total level entries.
Each level entry displays a locked or unlocked state consistent with progression.

requirements.description: Selecting and entering a level starts its 30-second countdown.
requirements.source_excerpt: Entering a level starts a 30-second countdown.
acceptance_criteria: On level entry the countdown begins at 30.0 seconds.
The countdown is visible during play.
The countdown starts only after the level scene is ready and player control begins.

requirements.description: The player can run, jump, and interact with switches and level objects.
requirements.source_excerpt:
The player runs, jumps, and
interacts with switches and objects.
acceptance_criteria: Horizontal movement responds to left and right input.
Jump input produces a jump when the player is grounded.
Interact input triggers eligible switches and interactive objects within range.

verification.rationale: Criterion 2: Level.handle_interact() is an empty function ('pass') and no interact-radius check exists, so the E action cannot trigger any switch or interactive object; this is an implementation defect against the current build.

requirements.description: At zero timer the screen flashes and rewinds; the player restarts at spawn while a translucent ghost replays the previous loop exactly.
requirements.source_excerpt:
When the timer hits zero, the screen
flashes and rewinds — the player restarts at the spawn point, but a translucent
ghost replays exactly what they did in the previous loop.
acceptance_criteria: A visible screen-flash effect occurs when the timer reaches zero.
The level rewinds the current player to the spawn point.
A ghost with alpha less than 1 is shown replaying the recorded previous loop.
The ghost reproduces the previous loop's player state sequence rather than a newly generated approximation.

requirements.description: Ghosts physically interact with the world by pressing buttons, holding doors, and blocking lasers.
requirements.source_excerpt:
The ghost physically
interacts with the world: it presses buttons, holds doors, and blocks lasers.
acceptance_criteria: A ghost overlapping a button or switch activates or holds it according to its type.
A ghost standing at a door or door-hold point keeps the door open for as long as the replay remains there.
A laser ray hitting a ghost is blocked at the ghost position instead of continuing to its normal target.

requirements.description: The player can layer up to four loops, producing at most four active ghost instances.
requirements.source_excerpt: The player can layer up to four loops.
acceptance_criteria: The loop manager permits no more than four active ghost instances.
The timeline and HUD represent each active ghost up to the four-loop maximum.
Attempting another loop after four active ghosts follows the defined maximum-loop reset behavior rather than creating a fifth ghost.

requirements.description: A top timeline bar shows all active ghosts and their current positions in the 30-second loop window.
requirements.source_excerpt:
A timeline bar at the top shows all
active ghosts and their current positions in the 30-second window.
acceptance_criteria: The play HUD includes a timeline bar spanning 0 to 30 seconds.
Each active ghost has a distinct marker on the timeline.
Each ghost marker updates to reflect that ghost's current playback time within the loop.

requirements.description: Touching the exit crystal completes the level only when all required switches are held by ghosts or the current player.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Reaching the
exit crystal with all required switches held (by ghosts or player) completes
the level.
acceptance_criteria: Each level defines the required switches needed for exit completion.
The exit crystal rejects completion while any required switch is unheld.
The exit crystal completes the level when all required switches are held by any combination of ghosts and the current player.

requirements.description: A reset button clears all ghosts so the player can start the level fresh.
requirements.source_excerpt: A reset button clears all ghosts to start fresh.
acceptance_criteria: The play HUD provides a visible reset button.
Activating reset removes all active ghosts.
Activating reset restarts the current level at its spawn point with a fresh 30-second timer and no retained loop replay.

requirements.description: The level-complete display reports loops used and the time of exit within the final loop.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Level-complete
shows loops used and time of exit within the final loop.
acceptance_criteria: The level-complete overlay shows an integer count of loops used.
The overlay shows the exit time within the final loop.
The displayed values match the completed session's loop count and final-loop exit timestamp.

requirements.description: The deliverable is a complete, shippable micro-game built in Godot 4 at /workspace/game, not a prototype.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Build **Time Loop**, a 30-second time loop platformer where past-self replays
help solve puzzles in Godot 4 at `/workspace/game/`. This is not a prototype.
It is a **complete, shippable micro-game** that could sit on an itch.io page or
Steam as a polished vertical slice.
acceptance_criteria: A Godot 4 project exists at /workspace/game.
The ordinary game path includes title, chapter menu, all 24 levels, loop rewinds, ghosts, timeline, reset, exit completion, and completion metrics.
Core gameplay does not depend on placeholder-only debug controls or an unfinished test scene.

verification.rationale: Criterion 2: Core gameplay is incomplete rather than shipped: handle_interact() is empty and procedural level data is a degenerate near-identical template with no temporal puzzles, so it does not meet the 'complete, shippable micro-game, not a prototype' bar.

requirements.description: 2D assets must be sourced from the mounted read-only Kenney CC0 library or OpenGameArt entries, respecting each OpenGameArt subdirectory license.
requirements.source_excerpt:
2D assets are mounted read-only at:

- `/workspace/assets/library/` — Kenney CC0 packs (sprites, tiles, UI, fonts).
- `/workspace/assets/library-oga/` — OpenGameArt entries; respect each
  subdir's `LICENSE.txt`.
acceptance_criteria: All imported visual assets come from the mounted asset libraries or from permissible engine primitives.
Kenney-sourced files are used as CC0 assets.
Any OpenGameArt-derived file is accompanied by or used in accordance with its subdirectory LICENSE.txt obligations.
No unlicensed external asset is introduced.

verification.rationale: Criterion 0: project-inventory lists only the asset paths, and the art manifest declares all 12 assets mock-image.v1 placeholders with both mounted libraries reported unavailable; imports are not sourced from the Kenney/OGA libraries.; Criterion 1: No file in the project is Kenney-sourced; all art files match the mock placeholder set, so no CC0 Kenney assets are used.

requirements.description: The implementer must browse the mounted libraries, choose suitable packs, and copy needed files into the project's assets folder.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Browse the library and choose packs.
Copy what you need into your project's `assets/` folder.
acceptance_criteria: Selected asset files are copied under /workspace/game/assets/.
Game scenes reference copied assets through project-relative res:// paths.
No gameplay asset is loaded from a read-only mount at runtime.

requirements.description: The Godot project layout must include project.godot, Main.tscn, demo_outputs, scripts, scenes, and assets under /workspace/game.
requirements.source_excerpt:
/workspace/game/
  project.godot
  Main.tscn
  demo_outputs/    <- your input traces (1-10 files)
  scripts/  scenes/  assets/
acceptance_criteria: /workspace/game/project.godot exists.
/workspace/game/Main.tscn exists as the entry scene.
/workspace/game/demo_outputs/, scripts/, scenes/, and assets/ exist.
The project opens and runs from this layout without missing-path errors for required scenes or assets.

verification.rationale: Criterion 2: scripts/, scenes/, and assets/ exist, but the project inventory contains no demo_outputs/ directory, so the required layout is incomplete.

requirements.description: The built project must launch cleanly with the specified headless command.
requirements.source_excerpt: godot --headless --path /workspace/game --quit-after 5
acceptance_criteria: Running the exact command exits without script parse errors or missing-resource errors.
The command completes within the five-second quit window.
The project creates no failure dialog or blocking startup error in headless mode.

requirements.description: Engine flags such as --headless and --quit-after N must precede the -- separator; user scenario arguments must come after --.
requirements.source_excerpt:
**Engine flags like `--headless` and `--quit-after N` must come BEFORE `--`** —
anything after `--` is forwarded to the project as user args and silently
ignored by the engine. Correct shape:
`godot --headless --quit-after 5 --path . -- --scenario near_victory`.
acceptance_criteria: Launch commands place --headless, --quit-after, and --path before --.
Scenario identifiers are placed after --.
Game code reads scenario identifiers from OS.get_cmdline_user_args rather than engine flags.

requirements.description: A screenshot helper at /workspace/tools/screenshot.sh is available and must be used to inspect UI and result screens.
requirements.source_excerpt:
A screenshot helper is available at `/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh`. Use it to actually see what your UI / battlefield /
result screens look like.
acceptance_criteria: Validation can invoke the helper with --path /workspace/game and --out to produce a screenshot.
The helper supports --frames and optional --scenario arguments.
Title, active-play, multi-ghost, and completion screens are inspected through rendered screenshots.

requirements.description: The project ships between 1 and 10 input-trace files under demo_outputs, one per demo, each named with a .json extension.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Ship **1-10 input-trace files** under `/workspace/game/demo_outputs/`, one per
demo, each named `*.json`.
acceptance_criteria: /workspace/game/demo_outputs/ contains at least 1 and at most 10 trace files.
Every trace file has the .json suffix.
Each demo has exactly one trace file and filenames are unique.

verification.rationale: Criterion 0: The deliverable project inventory contains no demo_outputs/ directory or trace files; player traces live in the player artifact area, not the packaged game.; Criterion 1: No .json trace files exist under the packaged demo_outputs/ per the project inventory.; Criterion 2: There are no packaged trace files, so the one-trace-per-demo uniqueness condition cannot hold in the delivery package.

requirements.description: The evaluator launches a fresh game per trace, replays synthetic mouse and keyboard input at 1280x720, records the screen, evaluates only the first 10 filenames, and samples recordings longer than 20 seconds.
requirements.source_excerpt:
The evaluator launches a fresh game per trace,
replays your trace as synthetic mouse and keyboard input at 1280x720, and
records the screen. Only the first 10 traces by filename are evaluated;
recordings longer than 20 s are sampled from a random 20 s window.
acceptance_criteria: Every trace is authored for the 1280x720 viewport.
Each trace can run from a fresh game launch without depending on prior process state.
No more than 10 trace files are shipped so that filename ordering does not exclude desired demos.
No demo depends on content outside a random 20-second sample if its recording exceeds 20 seconds.

verification.rationale: Criterion 2: No traces are shipped in the package, so the delivery set is empty and the 'no more than 10 traces' condition is not demonstrated.

requirements.description: Normal play starts at the title screen and demonstrates the core gameplay loop.
requirements.source_excerpt:
Normal play should start from the title screen and demonstrate the task's
core gameplay loop.
acceptance_criteria: A trace with no scenario begins on the title screen.
Accepting normal input from the title can reach the chapter menu and enter a level.
The demonstrated normal flow includes movement, timer expiry, ghost replay, and an exit attempt.

requirements.description: Demo playback must be deterministic.
requirements.source_excerpt: Demo playback must be deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Replaying the same trace from a fresh launch produces the same outcome.
Randomized elements are seeded or fixed for trace playback.
No timing-dependent setup varies between identical trace runs.

requirements.description: Demos that need a specific state must use named scenarios that the game loads when launched with a scenario argument.
requirements.source_excerpt:
For demos that need a specific state
(a specific level, combat state, upgrade screen, result state, or late-game
setup), define named scenarios your game loads when launched with:
acceptance_criteria: The project defines a finite set of named scenarios for level, loop, completion, and reset states.
Each scenario is selectable through the documented --scenario launch form.
Trace files may reference these scenario identifiers.

requirements.description: When a scenario argument is present, the game skips menus, sets up the named state deterministically, seeds any RNG, and immediately accepts input.
requirements.source_excerpt:
When `--scenario <id>` is present the game must skip menus, set up the named
state deterministically (seed any RNG), and begin accepting input immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario launch opens directly into the named gameplay or result state without title or chapter-menu steps.
Level selection, active loop count, ghost positions, and required switches match the scenario definition at frame zero.
All RNG used by the scenario is seeded deterministically.
Player input is accepted immediately after scenario setup.

requirements.description: A trace's scenario field is optional; omitting it means normal launch from the title screen.
requirements.source_excerpt: `scenario` — optional; omit for a normal game launch from the title screen.
acceptance_criteria: A trace without a scenario field launches the ordinary title flow.
A trace with a scenario field loads that named scenario.
Scenario omission does not produce a parse error.

requirements.description: The duration_frames field defines recorded frames at 30 fps with a maximum of 600 frames (20 seconds).
requirements.source_excerpt: `duration_frames` — total frames to record at 30 fps; cap at **600 (20 s)**.
acceptance_criteria: Every trace includes an integer duration_frames value.
No trace exceeds 600 frames.
Trace event frames are interpreted at 30 frames per second.

requirements.description: Trace events are time-ordered synthetic inputs with coordinates in the 1280x720 viewport and use the supported event types.
requirements.source_excerpt:
`events` — time-ordered inputs. Coordinates are pixels in the 1280x720
  viewport. Supported types:
acceptance_criteria: The events array is ordered by frame number.
Mouse coordinates lie within the 1280x720 viewport.
Only supported event types are used.

requirements.description: Keyboard trace events use one of the supported keycodes.
requirements.source_excerpt:
`A`-`Z`, `0`-`9`, `ESCAPE`, `ENTER`, `SPACE`, `TAB`, `BACKSPACE`,
    `DELETE`, `SHIFT`, `CTRL`, `ALT`, `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`.
acceptance_criteria: Every key event uses a listed keycode.
Keycodes outside the listed set are not emitted.
Held and released keys use matching supported keycodes.

requirements.description: Mouse drag traces use mouse_down at the start, one or more mouse_move events, and mouse_up at the end; a mouse_click is a down-up pair at the same point.
requirements.source_excerpt:
use these for drag interactions: emit `mouse_down` at the start point,
    one or more `mouse_move` events along the way, and `mouse_up` at the end.
    A `mouse_click` is a `mouse_down` + `mouse_up` at the same point in tight
    succession.
acceptance_criteria: A drag trace emits mouse_down before its mouse_move events and mouse_up after them.
Every mouse_move event lies between a matching down and up event.
A mouse_click event is replayable as down and up at the same coordinates.

requirements.description: A wait event has a frame and type only and acts as an anchor frame with no input.
requirements.source_excerpt: `wait`: `{frame, type}` — anchor frame, no input.
acceptance_criteria: Wait events contain no input payload beyond frame and type.
Wait events do not change game state.
Wait events can anchor timing between other events.

requirements.description: Replay must be deterministic: the same trace on a fresh launch must produce the same outcome every time.
requirements.source_excerpt: Replay must be deterministic: same trace, fresh launch, same outcome every time.
acceptance_criteria: Two identical fresh-launch replays of one trace produce the same final state and outcome.
No fresh-launch replay depends on mutable state from a prior replay.
Timing, ghost playback, and level completion are reproducible for the same trace.

issues.description: Player can leave the ground platform and fall unbounded with no out-of-bounds death or respawn, leaving the player unrecoverable and preventing completion attempts: near_rewind reaches y~34033 at frame 599 with velocity 8980 and near_victory reaches y~29004 at frame 450, both outside the 720-pixel view.
reproduction_steps: Run scenario near_rewind; step off the ground platform; observe Player position y growing past 540 without any respawn within 600 frames.
Run scenario near_victory; jump at frame 140 and move right; observe Player y beyond the platform with no recovery.

issues.description: Interact input is inert: Level.handle_interact() is empty and no interaction radius exists, so the E action cannot trigger switches or objects. Switches only react to body-overlap queries, never to the player's interact action as specified.
reproduction_steps: Inspect scripts/Level.gd handle_interact(): the body is 'pass'.
Launch a level, stand near a switch, send E; observe no switch state change.

issues.description: Ghost physical interactions are unverified by any mapped playthrough: no run places a ghost on a switch/pressure plate, holds a door, blocks a laser, or distracts an enemy while the player acts elsewhere. A mapped scenario transcript covering each interaction with observed held/door-open/enemy-distracted/beam-length state is required, and a run to four active ghosts with per-ghost timeline markers.
reproduction_steps: Provide a scenario and trace where a ghost occupies a switch and a plate while the player is distant; record ghost positions plus switches_held, door open, enemy distracted and laser beam length.
Drive a loop to four active ghosts and capture four distinct per-ghost timeline markers at different positions.

issues.description: The level-complete overlay path was never observed: no mapped playthrough drove the player to the exit crystal with all required switches held, so loops-used and final-loop exit time display remain unverified, and rejection-with-unheld-switch was never exercised.
reproduction_steps: Using scenario near_victory, provide a trace that touches the exit while s1 is unheld (expect rejected flash) and then when s1 is held; capture CompleteOverlay visible with LoopsLabel and TimeLabel values.

issues.description: Reset behavior is unverified: no mapped playthrough activates reset and confirms all ghosts are removed and the level restarts at spawn with a fresh 30-second timer and no retained replay. The reset_flow scenario exists but was never run.
reproduction_steps: Launch scenario reset_flow, click ResetButton (screen_rect 1080,8,184,40), and capture a frame where ghosts list is empty, tick=0, TimerLabel=30.00.

issues.description: Title trace replay is non-deterministic: title_nav_probe failed both fresh replays with state and pixel mismatch at frame 0, traced to TitleScreen.gd driving hand rotation from Time.get_ticks_msec(), a wall-clock source. Deterministic demo replay requires a fixed simulated clock for title animation.
reproduction_steps: Run title_nav trace twice from fresh launches; observe comparison:title_nav_probe-replay-1/2 status failed with first_state_difference=0 and first_pixel_difference=0.
Change TitleScreen animation to advance from a fixed simulated delta so title state is reproducible.

issues.description: Full 30-second loop duration from a fresh clock (expiry at exactly 30s) and ordinary level entry starting the countdown are unexercised; the 600-frame cap prevents a full loop from an ordinary start and all rewind evidence used preloaded scenarios. A clock-exposing run and a normal (no scenario) level-entry trace are needed.
reproduction_steps: Provide a scenario starting at tick=0 with TimerLabel 30.00 and capture the frame where tick crosses TICKS_PER_LOOP and TimerLabel reads 00.00 (or expose loop tick and verify expiry tick==900).
Provide a normal (no scenario) trace that clicks the Level 1 button rect [678,130,300,36] and captures level entry with TimerLabel 30.00.

issues.description: The screenshot helper usage requirement is unverified: no mapped evidence records invoking /workspace/tools/screenshot.sh with --path/--out/--frames/--scenario, and rendered title, active-play, multi-ghost and completion screens have not been pixel-inspected by this reviewer.
reproduction_steps: Run /workspace/tools/screenshot.sh --path /workspace/game -- --out <file> --frames N and with --scenario <id>, and supply the rendered captures for title, active play, multi-ghost and completion screens.

issues.description: A drag trace has never been exercised: no mouse_down/mouse_move/mouse_up drag segment exists in any supplied trace, so drag ordering and bracketed-move semantics could not be validated even though the game does not currently need drags.
reproduction_steps: Provide a trace with mouse_down at a start point, at least one mouse_move, and mouse_up after the moves, and confirm replay respects the bracketed ordering.

issues.description: Acceptance remains unverified. Collect or correctly map current evidence for the listed criteria; no missing test is claimed as a gameplay defect.
reproduction_steps: Review R002 criterion 2: Ghost positions advance with playback_frame, but no mapped evidence samples a ghost's recorded state against the contemporaneous recorded player stream to confirm frame-correspondence at the same loop time.

Review R004 criterion 0: No authored level data requires simultaneous contributions from two prior ghosts before the current player reaches the exit, and no mapped playthrough demonstrates such cooperation; this is an implementation/content defect needing a mapped scenario, not a contradiction of the instruction.

Review R004 criterion 1: Removing a ghost contribution is not shown to make the exit unreachable; the authored template uses independent switch/plate holds all reachable by the current player, so there is no observed removable ghost dependency.
Review R004 criterion 2: No mapped playthrough keeps multiple ghost contributions alive across successive loops to confirm persistence until reset or the loop ceiling.

Review R005 criterion 0: No mapped playthrough shows any level that cannot be solved in a single loop; the authored template is a collection of independent holds, but no run confirms single-loop solvability or non-solvability.

Review R005 criterion 1: No observed solution schedules distinct actions in different loop iterations at specified times; the shared template provides no cross-time dependency in the inspected data or snapshots.

Review R005 criterion 2: Earlier-loop ghost actions are not observed to be necessary for later-loop success in any mapped playthrough; only static level data is available and it does not encode this dependency.

readiness.rationale: Not ready. The build passes and a few requirements are evidenced (Godot 4 project layout except demo_outputs, clean headless launch, title first screen, four chapters of six level buttons, scenario skip-to-level and seeded entry, timer visible at 30.00, flash/rewind/respawn observed, several trace-format rules), but the game is not a shippable micro-game: the player falls out of the world (QA-002), interact is inert (QA-003), level content is a degenerate template with no temporal puzzles (QA-001), completion and reset were never observed (QA-005, QA-006), ghost interactions are unexercised (QA-004), the title trace is non-deterministic (QA-008), zero delivery traces are packaged (QA-007), and all art is mock placeholder (QA-010). Open blocker/major issues remain, and the host gates packaged_traces_replayed and final_art are false. Host abstained on 18 criterion decisions and withheld 3 issue updates. Host gate failures: packaged_traces_replayed, final_art, all_requirements_verified, no_blocking_issues, no_open_design_or_evidence_gaps.
